meta.title: GymPro · Training log with an AI coach
meta.description: Plan routines, log every set, and ask Ronnie, an AI coach that checks your actual workouts before it answers. In English and Traditional Chinese.

hero.title: A training log with a coach who reads it.
hero.body: Plan your routines, log every set, and ask Ronnie, GymPro's AI coach, whenever you're not sure what to do next. Ronnie looks at what you've actually trained before answering, and can adjust today's workout for you.

chat.label: Example chat: Ronnie suggests a substitute, and today's workout changes only when you tap Swap.
chat.subtitle: AI Personal Coach
chat.user: My lower back is tight today. Can I swap squats for something easier on it?
chat.reply: I'd swap Barbell Back Squat for Leg Press today: it's easier on your lower back. Go lighter than usual, and stop if it starts to hurt.
chat.swapped: ✓ Swapped "Barbell Back Squat" for "Leg Press" today

how.title: Plan, log, ask, review
how.intro: Four parts that feed each other: the more you log, the more Ronnie and your reports have to work with.

plan.title: Build routines and a cycle
plan.body: Pick exercises from the built-in library, set sets and reps, and arrange routines into a cycle of any length, rest days included. Or answer a few questions and let Coach G draft routines and a cycle for you to review before saving.

log.title: Log every set
log.body: The Today card opens on the day's routine from your cycle. Enter reps and weight as you go, in kg or lb, and add or drop exercises when plans change.

ask.title: Ask Ronnie
ask.body: Ronnie checks your workouts and routines before answering. It can add or swap exercises in today's workout, find an exercise from a description in English or Chinese, and suggest routine changes that only apply once you confirm.

review.title: Get a report every period
review.body: When a period ends (a week, or one full cycle), an AI Coach Report is written for you: training split, strength trend, progressive overload and what to do next, taking your notes for the period into account. History keeps past periods and your weight trend.

mock.planLabel: Example cycle: Push Day, Pull Day, Leg Day, then a rest day. Today is day 3, Leg Day.

mock.askLabel: Example: asking Ronnie for an upper-chest exercise and getting Incline Dumbbell Bench Press with an Add to today button.
mock.reviewLabel: Example AI Coach Report with a training split bar and a rising strength trend line.

researchText.lift_stalled: Adding reps and adding weight both work as progression; double progression adds reps first, then weight
researchText.lift_regressed: A short dip can be fatigue that recovery reverses; a drop that persists is the warning sign
researchText.deload: Deloading rests mostly on coaches' experience, with few trials; in one study a scheduled week off led to smaller strength gains
researchText.low_volume: More weekly sets build more muscle, with diminishing returns and no sharp threshold; 10 is GymPro's low-volume line, and 12–20 suits growing more
researchText.missed_sessions: A missed session costs that week's sets; with total sets equal, how often you train barely changes growth but does help strength
researchText.weight_trend: Losing 0.5–1% of body weight a week keeps more muscle on a cut; a modest surplus helps a bulk, but how much is unsettled

reportV3.accordionHint: Tap a row to open it; one opens at a time.
reportV3.musclesNote: {sets} working sets this {unit, select, week {week} other {cycle}}. Below: sets per muscle, scaled to a week. A muscle an exercise mainly trains counts a full set, one it trains on the side counts half: a bench press set is a chest set and half a triceps set. Front delts, calves and core have no range; presses already train the front delts.
reportV3.liftsNote: The best set each {unit, select, week {week} other {cycle}}; the line is the estimated 1RM over 6 {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}}. A lift counts as stalled after 3 flat {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}}.
reportV3.weighIns: {n, plural, one {# weigh-in} other {# weigh-ins}} this {unit, select, week {week} other {cycle}}
reportV3.weightWatch: Your goal is to {direction, select, gain {gain} other {lose}} weight, and it has gone {direction, select, gain {down} other {up}} {n} {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}} running; a note comes after {needed}.
reportV3.liftWatch: {lift} has been flat {n} {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}}; one more and it gets a note.

ruleText.lift_stalled: A main lift's best set hasn't improved for 3 {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}}
ruleText.lift_regressed: A main lift dropped 5% or more, or two {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}} in a row
ruleText.deload: Two or more main lifts dropped 3% or more, and more went down than up
ruleText.low_volume: Chest, back, side or rear delts, quads, hamstrings, glutes, biceps or triceps under 10 sets a week, and not just from a missed session
ruleText.missed_sessions: Days your training cycle planned that weren't trained
ruleText.weight_trend: Body weight moving against the goal 4 {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}} running

mainLifts.text: Lifts the goal names and each routine's first exercise, then the most-trained over the last 4 {unit, select, week {weeks} other {cycles}}; up to 5.

bestSet.text: The set with the highest estimated 1RM that {unit, select, week {week} other {cycle}}; reps for bodyweight exercises.

e1rm.text: A one-rep max estimated from weight and reps (Epley), so 80 kg × 10 and 85 kg × 6 can be compared.

record.text: A main lift's best set this {unit, select, week {week} other {cycle}} beat every earlier set.

weeklySets.text: Sets logged for each muscle, scaled to a week. A muscle an exercise mainly trains counts a full set, one it trains on the side counts half, the counting that fit the research best of those a meta-analysis compared. Shoulders are split into front, side and rear delts, and legs into quads and hamstrings, because different movements train them.

status.text: More main lifts up than down is progressing; the reverse is slipping; equal is holding steady.

reportV3.insufficient: Not enough sets were logged this period for a report.
